scheme_name: Scheme for Assistance for Research & Development Activities: Assistance for Contract/Sponsored Research Work
description:
The Scheme for Assistance for Research & Development Activities: Assistance for Contract/Sponsored Research Work was launched by the Government of India in 2018. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote research and development activities in various sectors. 

The scheme aims to enhance the quality and quantity of research output in India. 

It specifically targets industries and institutions that engage in contract or sponsored research work. 

The government seeks to foster collaboration between academia and industry through this initiative. 

The scheme also aims to provide financial assistance for research projects that have commercial viability. 

The measurable targets include increasing the number of research projects funded by 25 percent annually. 

Additionally, the scheme aims to improve the quality of research outputs by ensuring that at least 50 percent of funded projects result in publications in reputed journals. 

The financial benefits under this scheme can be substantial. 

The government provides assistance of up to 100 percent of the project cost. 

However, the maximum limit for funding is capped at INR 50 lakh per project. 

The funding is intended to cover various costs associated with research activities. 

These costs include equipment, consumables, and manpower. 

The eligibility criteria for applicants are clearly defined. 

Institutions of higher education recognized by the University Grants Commission are eligible to apply. 

Research and development organizations that are registered under the Societies Registration Act are also eligible. 

Private sector companies that are engaged in research activities can apply for this assistance. 

The applicants must have a proven track record in research and development. 

There is no specific age limit for applicants. 

However, the income criteria for private sector companies stipulate that they must have a turnover of at least INR 1 crore in the previous financial year. 

Educational qualifications are not explicitly mentioned. 

However, it is expected that the principal investigator should possess a doctoral degree in a relevant field. 

The application process is structured and requires several steps. 

First, applicants must prepare a detailed project proposal. 

This proposal should outline the objectives, methodology, and expected outcomes of the research. 

The proposal must also include a detailed budget breakdown. 

Once the proposal is prepared, it should be submitted to the relevant department of the Ministry of Science and Technology. 

The submission can be done online through the official government portal. 

Applicants must also provide supporting documents. 

These documents include proof of registration of the institution or organization. 

Additionally, a copy of the last three years of audited financial statements is required. 

The timeline for the application process is specified. 

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the year. 

However, applicants are encouraged to submit their proposals at least three months before the intended start date of the project. 

The disbursement of funds is typically done in installments. 

The first installment is released upon approval of the project proposal. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the project. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Science and Technology. 

They are responsible for evaluating the project proposals and monitoring the progress of funded projects. 

Contact details for the Department of Science and Technology can be found on their official website. 

The scheme has been instrumental in promoting innovation in various sectors. 

It has led to the development of new technologies and products that have commercial potential. 

Statistics indicate that since its inception, the scheme has funded over 200 projects. 

These projects span diverse fields such as biotechnology, information technology, and renewable energy. 

The government has reported a significant increase in collaboration between industry and academia as a result of this scheme. 

Moreover, the scheme has contributed to the creation of over 1,000 jobs in research and development. 

The impact of the scheme on the Indian economy is noteworthy. 

It has facilitated the commercialization of research outputs, leading to increased economic activity. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of intellectual property rights. 

Researchers are encouraged to file patents for their inventions. 

This is aimed at protecting the innovations developed through funded research. 

The government has established a framework for the commercialization of research outputs. 

This includes support for technology transfer and licensing agreements. 

The scheme aligns with the broader goals of the National Policy on Science and Technology. 

It seeks to position India as a global leader in research and innovation. 

The government regularly reviews the scheme to ensure its effectiveness. 

Feedback from stakeholders is taken into account for improvements. 

The scheme has received positive responses from various sectors. 

Many researchers have expressed appreciation for the financial support provided. 

They have noted that the assistance has enabled them to undertake ambitious projects. 

The scheme also encourages interdisciplinary research. 

This is crucial for addressing complex challenges facing society today. 

Overall, the Scheme for Assistance for Research & Development Activities: Assistance for Contract/Sponsored Research Work represents a significant investment in India's future. 

It underscores the government's commitment to fostering a culture of innovation and research excellence. 

The scheme is expected to evolve further to meet the changing needs of the research landscape. 

Future enhancements may include increased funding limits or expanded eligibility criteria. 

The government remains focused on ensuring that research contributes to national development goals. 

In conclusion, this scheme is a vital component of India's strategy to enhance its research capabilities. 

It provides essential support to researchers and institutions striving for excellence in research and development. 

The tangible benefits of the scheme are already evident in the growing number of successful projects and collaborations. 

As the scheme continues to develop, it promises to play a key role in shaping the future of research in India.
